data.title: Chat: AS-111 review residuals — a rename on the Docker Desktop bind mount replays the event stream twice (transient inode on the first stat), malformed counter survives resetTail after a re-read, and the watcher cut-close cycle (AC-7) has no red-capable test

data.body:
CONTEXT (qa-priya, filed from the AS-111 review, tick watcher:78911 loop tick 21). Three non-blocking findings from probing past AS-111's criteria list; none violates a stated criterion, all three are small and well-understood, so backlog not needs_human. Drivers in scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-111/ (probe.mjs, ino-diag.mjs, ac7-probe.test.mjs).

N1 — Docker Desktop bind mount: a rename over apps/chat/data/events/company.jsonl makes stat().ino report a TRANSIENT inode on the first poll after the rename and a different stable one on the next (measured inside the container against /app/data: 175276 -> 175277 -> 175279; container /tmp and the host both report one stable inode). tailEvents therefore resets twice and replays the whole file twice — every new-inode probe on the mount produced exactly 2x the company frames the host produced (a 2-line rotation: 4 frames; replay ids repeated twice). Reason 'replaced' and the fold are correct both times; a normal append never changes the inode, so no false 'replaced' on the append-only path. Fix shape: confirm an inode change on the following poll before resetting (one-poll debounce), or key the replacement on (ino changed AND bytes-before-cursor differ OR size < offset) with the inode alone treated as a hint. Test must run on a bind mount to see it (the compose test service is mountless by design) — a probe through the cli service with -v works; recipe in the AS-111 review comment.

N2 — resetTail() zeroes offset/partial/fold/lastId/lastTs/ino/lastBytes but NOT malformed. After a 'replaced' (or 'truncated') re-read, events.malformed still carries the count from the file that no longer exists (probe: 1 junk line, replaced by a file with 1 junk line -> malformed 2). Pre-existing on master for truncation; matters now because the 'replaced' sentence promises 'nothing is missing' and the counter says something else. One line: eventsTail.malformed = 0 in resetTail, plus an assertion in stream-company-replaced-same-inode that plants a junk line before the swap.

N3 — AC-7 ('the watcher's closeOpen stage_ended carries cycle from the open item') has no test that can go red: watcher-events-timeout-closes-as-cut's stageStartedEv plants cycle: null, and makeEvent fills a missing cycle with null, so deleting the 'cycle: stage.cycle ?? null' line leaves it green. Verified by direct probe that the value IS carried (cycle 3 read back off the cut close). Fix: plant cycle: 3 in that fixture (or a sibling) and assert ended.data.cycle === 3.

Priority low -> critical (Owen): Chat-set task, and the written scheduling rule (CLAUDE.md § Scheduling priority) has the whole set at critical so lattice next reflects it. Ordering inside the set stays by age.

Planned (cto-owen, tick watcher:57637 loop tick 22; planning lane on Opus under the Fable-limit fallback). Measured before deciding N1 (scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-124/): the bind-mount transient inode is TIME-based and non-deterministic, not one-stat — on the apps/chat/data mount one trial read the same new inode three times at 0 ms and a different one from 100 ms on with no second rename; 27 other trials across two mounts were stable from the first stat. Reproduced with AS-111's own test: stream-company-replaced-new-inode run in-container with its data dir on the apps/chat/data mount fails 6 !== 3 (master), green on a scratch-dir mount. So a count debounce narrows the window, and 'accept and document' would document a wrong premise (inode = identity). Decision N1: code fix — an inode change TRIGGERS a full-prefix compare (running sha256 of the consumed bytes vs a one-off hash of the new file's [0, offset)); equal → adopt the inode, no replay, reason untouched; different → replaced as today; inode change with size < offset → replaced (now pinned). Reason codes, sentences, lib/events.js, public/lanes.js untouched; both AS-111 replaced tests stay green by construction. N2: resetTail zeroes malformed, test asserts a RECOUNT (=== 1), not a zero. N3: test-only, stageStartedEv gains an optional cycle, new test reads cycle 3 off the cut close; the existing AC-7 test stays green under the mutant as the control. Five new tests: +4 stream.test.js, +1 watcher-events.test.js; predicted host 617/615/0/2, compose 617/609/0/8; bind-mount run of the five swap/replaced tests is AC-3 (branch green x3, master red 6!==3), counted on its own line. 8 anchored mutants with exact predicted red sets. Implementer Marcus (Lena is on AS-109 rework; plan carries the anchors); reviewer Ruben (Priya filed the findings and proposed the two shapes the plan rejects). Seams disjoint from AS-109/AS-125 (no api.test.js, no public/). Branch feat/AS-124-tail-prefix-confirm, worktree .worktrees/AS-124 at 7181486. Open: whether an identical-content swap should be said at all (default no), closes at review.

Implementation stage opened (Owen, tick watcher:57637 loop tick 23). Implementer: developer-lena — the plan's §7 Marcus pick was availability-based (Lena held the AS-109 rework lane at planning time); AS-109 is now in review, Marcus takes AS-125, so Lena takes this one. She wrote AS-111's tailEvents, which the plan notes as a trade-off: the second-pair-of-eyes benefit goes to Ruben's review instead. Order N3 -> N2 -> N1, commit early, scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-124/. Reviewer stays Ruben.

Implementation complete (developer-lena, Opus under the Fable fallback; plan §7 named Marcus for availability, lapsed — Lena implements, Ruben reviews). Branch feat/AS-124-tail-prefix-confirm, base 7181486, tip dece8c7. Four commits in plan §7 order: a89e994 N3 (test/watcher-events.test.js: stageStartedEv gains optional cycle=null, new watcher-events-cut-close-carries-cycle plants cycle 3 + a null-cycle sibling); 0720179 N2 (server.js resetTail zeroes malformed; stream-company-reset-recounts-malformed asserts ===1 after a truncate that re-reads one junk line); 64bf912 N1 (server.js: eventsTail.hash sha256 of every consumed byte incl. partial, reset with the tail; prefixMatches(fd, offset) streams [0,offset) in 64 KiB reads; tailEvents: confirmIno flag — size<offset at a new inode → replaced outright (ahead of the size rule), else the fd is opened and the prefix compared: equal adopts the inode with cursor/fold/reason untouched and skips the window check, different → replaced; the size===offset early return moved below the compare, so an adopted swap with nothing new closes the fd and returns [] via a chunk===null branch; the inode is adopted only after the compare passes or a reset — an unreadable file on the confirming poll leaves it pending for the next one (plan §6 e). Tests: stream-company-swap-identical-prefix-adopts, -with-partial, stream-company-replaced-shorter-new-inode); dece8c7 README (AC-6 paragraph: inode change confirmed against the consumed prefix, identical swap adopted without replay, Docker Desktop bind-mount transient inode named as the reason, residual sentence stands, 'malformed counts the file currently folded' clause). Files touched: server.js, README.md, test/stream.test.js, test/watcher-events.test.js — nothing else; git diff --exit-code master... on lanes.js/events.js/bin/events.js/advance-watcher.mjs/compose.yaml/api.test.js/roster-truncation.test.js is empty (AC-2). Open question §9.2 closed at implementation with the default: the window check does not run when the prefix compare passed. COUNTS. Host base 612/610/0/2 (agrees with §0). Compose base asc-impl-as124: 'Image asc-impl-as124-test Built' 612/604/0/8. Host tip 617/615/0/2. Compose tip: 'Image asc-impl-as124-test Built' tests=617 pass=609 fail=0 skipped=8 — both exactly §5. merge-tree --write-tree master..branch clean (dee8e38). MUTANTS (§3, scratch detached worktree /tmp/AS-124-mutant, never the task worktree; each edit anchored to exact line text + asserted inside the enclosing function's line span, hunk printed, full host suite per run, checkout + git diff --exit-code clean after each): cardinality 8 runs; 8 red, 0 survivors, 0 mismatches vs the predicted sets. M1 (if(true) at the prefixMatches call, server.js:487) → {swap-identical-prefix-adopts, swap-identical-prefix-with-partial}, 617/613/2/2, first failure 'an identical-content swap replays nothing'. M2 (if(false), same site) → {replaced-new-inode}, 'the whole new file is re-read: three lines, three frames'. M3 (window-only compare at the same site) → {replaced-new-inode}, same line — full prefix is load-bearing. M4 (hash.update moved from the read step :512 to complete lines at the parse step :535) → {swap-identical-prefix-with-partial}, 'adopted: no replay'. M5 (resetTail('truncated') at :473) → {replaced-shorter-new-inode}, 'a shorter file at a new inode is a rotation, not a truncation'. M6 (delete malformed=0 in resetTail :391) → {reset-recounts-malformed}, 'recounted from the new file: its one junk line, not the old file's too'. M7 (delete advance-watcher.mjs:2275 anchored on the AS-111 F4 comment) → {cut-close-carries-cycle}; control watcher-events-timeout-closes-as-cut GREEN, which is N3's finding reproduced. M8 (cycle: null hard-coded) → {cut-close-carries-cycle}. One deviation to record: my first battery pass printed 8 'MISMATCH' labels — the driver's parser counted node's ✖ lines twice (inline plus the 'failing tests:' summary); the fail= counts were correct throughout; parser fixed, re-run, clean log in scratchpad/agent-developer-lena/AS-124/mutants.log. BIND MOUNT (AC-3, separate from the compose receipt; docker 29.6.1 via /usr/local/bin/docker; node:24-slim, branch apps/chat mounted :ro, TMPDIR on the MAIN checkout's apps/chat/data mount — the one asc-chat-server-1 shares, which is the mount §0.1 says misbehaves; the worktree's own data dir is not that mount — scratch subdir as124-lena-scratch, gitignored, removed after): branch run 1/3 tests=5 pass=5 fail=0; run 2/3 5/5/0; run 3/3 5/5/0 — three of three green. Master run: tests=2 pass=1 fail=1 (only the two AS-111 replaced-* tests exist there), red stream-company-replaced-new-inode 'three lines, three frames' actual 6 expected 3 — the falsifier reproduces. Left undone: nothing in scope. For the reviewer (M6 leads): (1) the early-return restructure — read tailEvents cold and say whether the confirmIno/chunk===null shape is legible; I kept the reason housekeeping duplicated in the two return sites rather than extracting a helper, to keep the diff inside the function; (2) prefixMatches treats a short read (file shorter than offset at read time — a race between stat and open) as a mismatch → replaced; (3) hash cost on an 8 MiB prefix (§6 d) I did not time; (4) the mv+cp rotation with a no-stream gap (§6 a) is unchanged: no-stream resets the hash, so the cp reads as a fresh file from 0 with one replay, reason no-stream → ok, not replaced. Cleanup: scratch worktree removed, worktree status clean, compose-run --check no asc-*as124* leftovers. Status untouched — Owen moves it.

in_progress -> review (Owen, tick watcher:57637 loop tick 23, --no-auto-review). Lena's lane ran on Opus under the Fable fallback. Branch tip dece8c7 (4 commits, N3 -> N2 -> N1 -> README); host 617/615/0/2, compose asc-impl-as124 Built 617/609/0/8; 8 mutants 0 survivors 0 mismatches; bind-mount line branch 3/3 green 5/5/0, master 2/1/1 red on stream-company-replaced-new-inode 6!==3. Reviewer: qa-ruben per §7 (fresh context; do not read Lena's comment or scratchpad before forming findings).

REVIEW (qa-ruben, cycle 1, on Opus under the Fable-limit fallback) — verdict: implementation-level rework needed. One finding (F1, a missing host guard on a load-bearing line of N1); every acceptance criterion passes; the implementation itself is correct as far as I could break it. I read the plan and the diff cold and wrote this before reading Lena's implementation comment; the reconciliation note is at the end.

FINDINGS (first; 1 defect, 2 observations, 1 out-of-scope doc note) — reproductions in scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-124/ (mutants.cjs, mutants-M1-M8.log, mutants-R.log, probe.mjs, probe-r11.mjs, mount-run.cjs, compose.out, master-mount-fail.log).

F1 — DEFECT (test-coverage, implementation-level). `resetTail`'s `eventsTail.hash = createHash('sha256')` (server.js 394) is load-bearing for N1 on the deployed mount and no host or compose test sees it. Mutant R11 (delete that one line; anchor `lastBytes = Buffer.alloc(0)\n    eventsTail.hash = createHash(...)` inside resetTail, hunk @@ -393 printed) SURVIVES the full host suite: 617/615/0/2, red set = {}. It is not an equivalent mutant: probe-r11.mjs (genuine rotation to a longer file at a new inode, then an identical-content swap at another new inode — the sequence the Docker Desktop mount produces when a real rotation is followed by its transient inode flap) gives on the branch {afterRotation: 3 frames, replaced; afterFlap: 0 frames, replaced} and under R11 {afterRotation: 3, replaced; afterFlap: 3, replaced} — the N1 double replay, back through the reset path, because the stale hash covers old+new bytes and the flap's prefix compare mismatches. Why it slipped: both new swap tests start from a fresh boot (never reset), so the running hash was never stale when the swap arrived. The only guard today is AC-3's bind-mount run of `stream-company-replaced-new-inode`, which is environment-only and non-deterministic (master went red 6 of 9 runs, below). Argued from M4 (CLAUDE.md): the plan states "an inode that flaps forever costs one prefix hash per flap and never a replay" as a property, and its host falsifier covers only the no-prior-reset half. Rework: one host test in stream.test.js, same shape as `-swap-identical-prefix-adopts` — appendTwoLines, drain 2; rename a longer different-prefix file over the path (a genuine `replaced`, 3 frames); then swapIdentical(path); drain → 0 company frames, reason still `replaced` (one lifecycle: it stays until the next append), malformed 0; then one append → exactly 1 frame and reason `ok`. Its mutant is R11 above; the implementer observes it red and quotes the set. No production change. Suggested id: `stream-company-replaced-then-identical-swap-adopts`.

O1 — observation, not a finding. R9 (`if (size === eventsTail.offset && !confirmIno)` → drop `&& !confirmIno`, i.e. master's early return, hunk @@ -477) survives: 617/615/0/2. It is behaviourally equivalent for everything served: the confirm is deferred to the first poll with new bytes and runs against the file at that moment, which is correct either way. The only divergences are an in-place truncation of the adopted-but-unconfirmed file reading `replaced` instead of `truncated`, and an unreadable new file at size === offset reading `ok` instead of `unreadable-stream` — neither worth a test. Recording it so nobody reads the "structural cost" paragraph in the plan as a guarded property: it is a design preference (confirm promptly), and R9 says the suite cannot tell.

O2 — observation, not a finding. R13 (`if (!confirmIno) eventsTail.ino = ino;` → unconditional, hunk @@ -476: adopt the inode before confirming) survives: 617/615/0/2. Observable only if the confirming poll's open fails (EACCES) on a different-content swap whose window matches — then the branch confirms next poll and says `replaced`, R13 adopts silently and misses it. chmod 000 mid-rotation is not a sequence an operator produces; the comment at 467–470 states the intent correctly. Left as-is.

N1 — out of scope, doc-only, pre-existing from AS-111 (for the orchestrator to file or fold into a doc pass). README § "Company events" residual sentence says "same inode, same size, and an edit before the last 64 bytes is not noticed". The algorithm's blind spot is wider than the English: same inode, ANY size >= offset, edit before the window. Falsifier (probe j): same inode, in-place rewrite that changes line 1 and appends a third line (longer) — reason `ok`, 1 company frame, no replay; the README's "same size" qualifier says nothing about this case. server.js 434–437 has the same wording. One clause: drop "same size". Not this branch's change (AC-6 says the residual sentence stands, and it does).

FLOOR CHECK (second; findings outside the list: 1 defect + 2 observations + 1 doc note, above) — 7 of 7 acceptance criteria pass.
AC-1 (N1 host): the three swap tests pass; M1–M5 each observed red with exactly the predicted set (tally below).
AC-2 (no regression): `stream-company-replaced-new-inode`, `-replaced-same-inode`, `stream-company-truncation`, `lanes-label-events-reason-table` unmodified (test diff touches none) and green; `git diff master... --stat` is exactly README.md, server.js, stream.test.js, watcher-events.test.js — lib/events.js and public/lanes.js untouched.
AC-3 (bind mount): my own driver (mount-run.cjs — node:24-slim, branch apps/chat mounted :ro at /app, TMPDIR on a gitignored scratch dir under apps/chat/data, the dir the running asc-chat-server-1 mounts; removed after). Branch, five tests (`replaced-new-inode`, `replaced-same-inode`, `replaced-shorter-new-inode`, `swap-identical-prefix-adopts`, `swap-identical-prefix-with-partial`): bind mount 5/5/0/0 — three of three runs. Master, same driver (only the two AS-111 tests exist there, cardinality 2, then 1 in the detail runs): red on 6 of 9 runs, always `stream-company-replaced-new-inode` at stream.test.js:1114 "the whole new file is re-read: three lines, three frames — 6 !== 3", verbatim in master-mount-fail.log. The falsifier counts; the non-determinism the plan predicted is real (first three master runs were 2 green, 1 red).
AC-4 (N2): resetTail zeroes malformed (server.js 391); `stream-company-reset-recounts-malformed` green; M6 red = {that test} only.
AC-5 (N3): `watcher-events-cut-close-carries-cycle` green; M7 and M8 each red = {that test} only; `watcher-events-timeout-closes-as-cut` stayed green under M7 (fail count 1) — the control that shows the AS-111 gap was real. Sweep path (plan §6 g): probe drove a 31-minute-old stage with cycle 2 through `sweep()`; the close carries cycle 2, outcome cut_by_timeout, closedBy watcher-sweep.
AC-6 (docs): README 636–649 says the inode change is confirmed against the consumed prefix, an identical swap is adopted without replay, names the Docker Desktop bind mount's transient inode as the reason, keeps the residual sentence, and carries the one-clause malformed sentence. public/lanes.js not edited.
AC-7 (counts): below, with the Built line.

COUNTS. Host (`node --test` in .worktrees/AS-124/apps/chat): 617 tests / 615 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped — plan §5 predicted 617/615/0/2. Compose (`node apps/chat/bin/compose-run.mjs --project asc-review-as124 --cwd .worktrees/AS-124/apps/chat`): "built: Image asc-review-as124-test Built"; tests=617 pass=609 fail=0 skipped=8; run exit 0, down exit 0, leak check clean — plan predicted 617/609/0/8. Bind mount (separate line, never folded in): branch 5 tests, 5/5/0/0 ×3; master 2 tests → `replaced-new-inode` red 6 of 9 runs, 6 !== 3. `--check` after: no asc-*as124* leftovers.

MUTANT TALLY. Cardinality: 8 plan mutants + 3 of mine = 11 runs, each on a scratch detached worktree at dece8c7 (/tmp, outside the scanned tree), anchor asserted to match exactly once, hunk printed with its line, full host suite, `git checkout -- .` then `git diff --exit-code` clean after every run. Plan mutants: 8 of 8 red, 8 of 8 with exactly the predicted set — M1 {swap-adopts, swap-with-partial} (both AS-111 replaced tests stayed green, as predicted); M2 {replaced-new-inode}; M3 (window-only compare on inode change) {replaced-new-inode} — full prefix is load-bearing; M4 (hash complete lines only) {swap-with-partial}; M5 {replaced-shorter-new-inode}; M6 {reset-recounts-malformed}; M7 {cut-close-carries-cycle}; M8 {cut-close-carries-cycle}. Mine: R9 survived (equivalent, O1), R11 survived (real, F1), R13 survived (contrived, O2). Zero wider or narrower sets.

M6 PROBES past the list (plan §6 a–g plus h–j of mine; probe.mjs against the branch server, 25 ms polls unless stated): (a) `mv` then `cp` with a poll in the gap: gap reads `no-stream`, after the cp 2 frames replayed and reason `ok` — one replay, `no-stream → ok`, the plan's default; I agree an operator gets nothing from a new reason code here (§9.1 default no stands; §9.3: a README clause recommending `cp` then `mv` is fine but not required). (a') `mv`+`cp` inside one 300 ms poll gap: 0 frames, `ok` — adopted. (b) two renames in one gap, second with different line 1: 3 frames, `replaced` — compared once against the second file. (c) longer swap, identical prefix, new bytes ending mid-line: 0 frames, malformed 0, `ok`; completing the line → 1 frame, malformed 0. (d) 8 MiB identical swap adopted with 0 frames; the compare costs 8.3 ms on host tmp and 21–30 ms in-container on the apps/chat/data bind mount, against a 2000 ms EVENTS_POLL_MS. (e) size === offset with a pending inode change and an unreadable (mode 000) new file: `unreadable-stream`, no throw; chmod back → `ok`, 0 frames (adopted, cursor kept); one append → 1 frame. (f) no-stream → file appears: reasons over the next six polls all `ok`, 1 frame — no spurious `replaced`. (g) above under AC-5. (h) identical swap while `replaced` is pending its next append: 0 frames and the reason stays `replaced` — one lifecycle honoured. (i) empty file adopted at a new inode, then a one-line file at another new inode: 0 frames `ok`, then 1 frame `ok` (offset 0: nothing consumed, nothing to compare). (j) same-inode in-place rewrite, longer, line 1 changed, window identical: `ok`, 1 frame — the AS-111 residual, wider than the README says (N1 above).

Legibility of the restructured `tailEvents` (plan §7 asked): readable cold. `confirmIno` as "the compare is still owed" with the two adoption sites (477 for the no-change case, 491 after the compare) is the one thing to hold in your head, and the comment at 467–470 says it. `chunk === null` is reachable only via an adopted swap with nothing past the cursor — I traced the other paths (a reset leaves offset 0 against a size that the earlier `size === offset` return already excluded unless confirmIno; an empty file adopted at offset 0 matches trivially) and the comment at 505 is true. No inline changes made.

Seams: master moved 6fc31b1 → 8e68358 during the review (board state and a records export only); `git merge-tree --write-tree master feat/AS-124-tail-prefix-confirm` clean before and after (adaf61e). AS-125 and AS-126 touch test/api.test.js and public/ — disjoint from this branch's four files. Worktree clean at dece8c7.

VERDICT: implementation-level rework needed — F1 only: add the rotation-then-identical-swap host test and observe R11 red; nothing else changes. O1/O2 need no action; N1 is for the orchestrator to route.

Reconciliation with Lena's comment (read after the above was written): every count agrees — host 617/615/0/2, compose Built 617/609/0/8, 8/8 plan mutants with the same red sets, bind mount branch 3/3 and master red at the same assertion. Her battery did not include R11 (it is outside plan §3), so F1 is new, not a re-record. Her M6 leads: (1) legibility — answered above, legible; (2) a short read in prefixMatches (file shorter than offset between stat and open) reads as `replaced` — correct, that file cannot hold the consumed prefix; (3) hash cost — timed above, 21–30 ms on the mount; (4) the mv+cp gap — confirmed above, one replay, `no-stream → ok`. Her §9.2 close (window check skipped after a passed compare) is what I read in the code and is right.

Lena addresses Ruben's F1 (plan § Review Cycle 1 Findings: one host test stream-company-replaced-then-identical-swap-adopts whose mutant is R11, observed red) in .worktrees/AS-124 on feat/AS-124-tail-prefix-confirm. Ruben reviews cycle 2 next tick.

Cycle 2 implementation (developer-lena, on Opus — Fable refused the spawn at HTTP 429; tick watcher:79108 loop tick 1). Scope: Ruben F1 only — one host test, no production change.

FINDINGS OUTSIDE F1: none. Two observations, neither a defect: (1) under R11 the new test fails at its FIRST post-swap assertion (company frames after the identical swap: actual 3, expected 0), i.e. the whole replayed file replays a second time — the exact N1 double replay Ruben's probe-r11 described, now reproduced on the host without a bind mount; (2) reason stays 'replaced' across the adoption and clears on the next append — one lifecycle, as Ruben's comment expected; the test pins that ordering.

CHANGE: apps/chat/test/stream.test.js +1 test, 'stream-company-replaced-then-identical-swap-adopts', placed after '-swap-identical-prefix-with-partial' in the N1 block. Shape as specified: appendTwoLines, drain 2; rename a LONGER different-first-line file over the path (new inode; precondition asserts the consumed prefix differs) → 3 frames, reason 'replaced'; swapIdentical(path) → 0 company frames, reason still 'replaced', malformed 0; one laneless append → exactly 1 frame with that id, reason 'ok'. Reuses the same-inode test's fixture bytes and the existing swapIdentical helper.
